summary: FBRX 2.4.0 Beta (Weft): Fabrix’s personality with ready-made personas, a network check that finds where the internet stops, remote desktop to your other computers, and This PC.
notes: Personality (Settings → Personality, it was Soul): ready-made personas such as Everyday helper and IT pro, and your options as simple fields. FBRX’s own principles (privacy, secrets, no harm, asking first) always come first, whatever the persona says.
Setup asks what you will be using FBRX for and picks a persona and AI Toolkit actions to match; Settings → Personality and AI Toolkit change them later.

Network Center → Check every layer: finds where a network stops working, from the adapter and Wi-Fi up to websites, with what to do first. Fabrix runs the same check when you ask why the internet is down, and has new skills for printers, sound, Bluetooth, screens and USB.

Remote desktop (RDP) and screen sharing (VNC) beside SSH and Telnet (Ultra): from a scanned device or New connection in Terminal → Device consoles, in your computer’s own viewer, which asks for the password. Kept in Saved connections.

This PC (first in Pit Stop): the make and model, serial number, processor, each memory module, drives and their health, graphics, screens, network adapters and battery, with Copy all and a link to the page that looks after each part.
Glass is now called Home in the sidebar.
Every notification has a close button, and Clear all clears them at once.
FBRX/1 shows your edition (Essentials, Pro, Ultra or Black Hole Edition).
Fabrix’s instructions are shorter, so small local models answer sooner.
Prices: Ultra is now $24.99 a month and Black Hole Edition $49.99; Pro stays $4.99.

server.summary: FBRX Server 1.4.3 comes with FBRX OS 2.3.3 and changes nothing on the server itself: updating from 1.4.2 is optional.
notes: The same server as 1.4.2, released alongside FBRX OS 2.3.3.
From 1.1: sudo fbrx-server update check, then sudo fbrx-server update commit.

digger.summary: FBRX Digger 1.2.0: Check every layer finds where a network stops working, and remote desktop opens beside the consoles.
notes: Overview → Check every layer: from the adapter and Wi-Fi signal through the router, the address, routing, names (DNS) and secure connections up to websites, with what to do first and the commands that show each layer by hand.
Remote desktop (RDP) and screen sharing (VNC) from a scan or New connection, in your computer’s own viewer, which asks for the password. They go in Saved connections like the consoles.
